material.acceptance_criteria: After a mod edit is hot-reloaded on the server, every connected client applies the new mod data without a page reload within one second, and a rejected reload leaves the client on its previous data.
material.description: rust/crates/web/site/main.js:55 fetches map.bin once and rust/crates/web/site/main.js:53-57 loads pkg/web.js once; there is no subscription or update channel. Server hot reload with rollback (rust/crates/mod-host/src/lib.rs) therefore never reaches a running client, so the low-latency HMR the goal asks for stops at the server.
material.resolution: Browser polls /mod-events and refetches map.bin on a version change, updates data-mod-version, keeps the last good game when a reload is rejected, and stops after MOD_MAX_FAILURES rejected reloads. CI covers a valid edit (1 to 2) and a server-side rejection with the canvas still present. Gap: the browser-side rejected counter is not triggered by CI, because the server does not publish a version for a broken mod.
material.subject: Connected browser clients never receive a mod or map update; only the server reloads
material.witness: ci-status run 38897564512 for 6b44b27f818f32461ca66dc84470712ec5c7e2c3; main.js watchMod rejected counter lines 259-283; CI broken-mod and server-rejection checks
material.witness_plan: CI step runs the server and a headless browser, edits a mod in the harness, and asserts the client's data version attribute changes and that a rejected edit leaves it unchanged.
